libs.note: BH-9354 (2026-11-13). A triage tick mints one App token and exports it, and bin/gh-ledger/gh only picks an identity when GH_TOKEN is empty, so a token that went bad stayed in the session (2026-11-09: four triage sessions got HTTP 401 while the box credentials answered 200). triage_gh_session_arm (bin/lib/triage-gh-token.sh) puts bin/gh-session/gh first on the tick's PATH; it re-mints the armed token per call, tries gh-token.sh --fresh and then env/gh-pat on a 401, and on a 401 from every credential writes one [gh-session] alert with the box's own probe and a marker that makes call_guard_finish settle the tick unbilled. Resolved once per tick by the arm (lib_env_apply gh-session) and exported. Off switch: the GH_SESSION_REMINT row (0). There is no flags/ file.

knobs.note: 1 = a triage tick arms bin/gh-session/gh. 0 = no arming: the session's gh runs on the tick's token as before BH-9354. Read as ${GH_SESSION_REMINT:-1}.

Life the cached App token must still have to be handed to a session gh call (bin/gh-token.sh --min-life). The same 600 as GH_APP_DEFAULT_MIN_LIFE_S, so one cache row serves both. Read as ${GH_SESSION_MIN_LIFE_S:-600}.
The longest one bin/gh-token.sh call inside the wrapper may take before the call keeps the token it has. Read as ${GH_SESSION_MINT_TIMEOUT_S:-15}.
The longest each box-probe GET repos/<slug> may take on the all-401 path (one on a box App token, one on env/gh-pat). Read as ${GH_SESSION_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S:-10}.
One [gh-session] ALERTS line per repo slug per this window (stamp state/gh-session.alerted/<slug>). 0 = every all-401 call alerts. Read as ${GH_SESSION_ALERT_EVERY_S:-3600}.
1 = after a 401 on both App rungs the call is tried once on env/gh-pat (it then acts as the PAT's user). 0 = no PAT rung; the box probe still reads env/gh-pat. Read as ${GH_SESSION_PAT_FALLBACK:-1}.
